messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High 5xx rate detected on api-gateway (eu-west-1). Alert: gateway-5xx-rate > 5% for 5m. PagerDuty incident #PD-8241 created.
incident-bot: Auto-run playbook: https://redwood.internal/ops/playbooks/api-gw-5xx (runbook id: pb-api-gw-5xx)
Leah (oncall): I'm on it — Leah taking pager. Quick check: is this regional or global?
Diego (gateway): Seeing a sharp spike starting ~1759993200. 502/504s concentrated on eu-west edge nodes. Dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/api-gateway?org=redwood&region=eu-west-1
Ashwin (infra): Linking top alert: connection_pool_exhausted on auth-service upstream. 10k rps → 5xx went from 0.2% to 18% in ~3m.
Maya (sre): Copy. Running quick upstream check on one affected gateway host:
Maya (sre): ```
$ ssh gw-eu-12
$ sudo tail -n 50 /var/log/nginx/error.log[error] 1234#0: *98765 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.45, server: api.redwood.com, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.5.8.12:8080/", host: "api.redwood.com"
```
Priya (support): Getting customer DMs: "requests failing with 502s since 08:45 UTC". A few large accounts reporting degraded UX. I'll open CS incident and gather customer IDs.
Leah (oncall): Initial impact classification: P1 (customer-facing, significant error surface). Triage plan: (1) isolate cause (upstream auth vs gw), (2) apply traffic fallback / rate-limit heavy callers, (3) scale or restart failing upstreams, (4) monitor.
Diego (gateway): Heatmap by upstream: auth-service shows 90% of 502s. Backend status health-checks 200-> intermittently 502. Might be connection storm after certificate rotation? Not sure.
Ashwin (infra): I see a recent cert rotation job for internal mTLS at 1759990000. Possible mismatch on a subset of nodes. Checking envoy/sidecar logs now.
Maya (sre): Quick synthetic:
Maya (sre): ```
$ curl -v https://auth.internal.svc.cluster.local/health 
* Connected to auth.internal.svc.cluster.local (10.5.8.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake has read 0 and written 1959
* SSL: certificate verify ok
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"upstream_error"}
```
Maya (sre): Auth pods are up but responding 502 for some requests. kube restarts low but high latency on connections.
Ashwin (infra): Running `kubectl describe` shows connection errors in auth pods: `failed to accept connection: too many open files`. Looks like file descriptor exhaustion on auth-service.
Leah (oncall): Mitigation actions: 1) temporarily enable backup auth path (stateless token validation fallback) on gateway to reduce load on auth-service. 2) rate-limit heavy callers (identify top 10 clients by rps). 3) scale auth-service replicas and increase ulimit in pod spec.
Diego (gateway): Rolling a gateway config change to enable fallback token validation (canary to 10% traffic first). Deploying now.
Diego (gateway): ```
# envoy config snippet applied via config-manager
route: 
  - match: /v1/*
    retry_policy: disabled
    fallback_auth: local_token_check
```
Diego (gateway): Canary applied to gw-eu-10..12 (10% traffic). Monitoring error rates.
Maya (sre): Scaling auth-service from 3 -> 8 replicas and bumping container ulimits. Applying now: 
Maya (sre): ```
kubectl scale deployment/auth-service -n infra --replicas=8
kubectl patch deployment auth-service -n infra --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"auth","securityContext":{"runAsUser":1000},"resources":{"limits":{"cpu":"500m"}}}]}}}}'
```
Ashwin (infra): Also bumping host-level file limits on affected nodes via chef run (uploader job). Pushing change to eu-hostpool-2.
Priya (support): Customers reporting intermittent improvement for a subset of requests. Still noisy. I've informed key accounts and queued outbound comms.
Leah (oncall): Applying temporary rate limit: 100rps per token for top callers. Diego, can you block the known bulk-batch client that spiked at 08:44?
Diego (gateway): Blocking client key ck-0xBATCH on gw-eu, applying rate limit and soft-503 for excessive requests. 
Diego (gateway): ```
# quick block
POST /admin/ratelimit
{"client_id":"ck-0xBATCH","limit_rps":10,"mode":"soft-503"}
```
Maya (sre): After scaling & fallback canary: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 4.7% in 4 minutes. Good signal.
Leah (oncall): Can someone confirm auth-service logs for fd exhaustion cleared after ulimit bump?
Ashwin (infra): Confirmed: new ulimit effective, no more `too many open files` in last 2m. Restarts normalized.
Maya (sre): Full revert of canary fallback planned once auth stabilizes. Keep canary at 10% until we're steady.
Priya (support): CS: Logged impacted accounts and ETA for follow-up: 2h. Customers want incident summary when resolved.
Diego (gateway): Monitoring global error budget and latencies. P95 latency unchanged. 502 tail fell back to baseline after 9 mins of mitigation.
Leah (oncall): Current status: impact reduced, mitigation in place (fallback + scale + rate-limit). Assigning post-incident follow-up to infra & gateway to root-cause cert/rotation + fd tuning.
Leah (oncall): Handoff: I'm going to hand to Ashwin for long-term fixes. I'll stay available for questions.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-8241 state changed -> acknowledged by Leah.
Ashwin (infra): Taking ownership for RCA and remediation tasks: will open a GH issue and include steps to prevent fd exhaustion (ci-tests, kube liveness thresholds, alert thresholds).
Maya (sre): Quick checklist for postmortem: timeline, root cause (fd exhaustion triggered by cert rotation edge-case), mitigation timeline, customer impact, action items.
Priya (support): I'll draft customer-safe summary and coordinate with communications.
Leah (oncall): Thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated. Will update incident channel once RCA doc is ready. :thumbsup:
Diego (gateway): :shipit:
Maya (sre): Adding logs + graphs to the incident page: https://incidents.internal/PD-8241
Leah (oncall): Closing active pager. Follow-up owner: Ashwin (infra).
